name: format-migration
body: Format migration: the definition of one ordered, versioned step that carries a kalide project from one format/version to the next — for a template library, a `library.yaml` `format:` bump and the schema rewrites it governs; across kalide versions, a `template.yaml` (or deck-config) schema change. Each migration is defined by kalide and names its source and target version; it is applied at most once, in order, by the upgrade-project service (domain.service.upgrade-project), and preserves the author's values (a library's `name`/`description`, a deck's title/author/date/properties) while changing only the format/structure it governs. Migrations are not guessed from the project's files: a format with no defined migration (unknown, or newer than the running kalide) is reported, not migrated (global.constraint.upgrade-unknown-format-reported). The result of a migration is validated before it is kept; a multi-file migration is all-or-nothing, so a failed step leaves the project unchanged (global.constraint.upgrade-never-breaks-project). The registered set is empty today: there is no format older than `1`, so a current project is a no-op. A migration is a rule kalide authors — it has no occurrence identity of its own and nothing is recorded when one is applied — so it is a value of the upgrade domain, realising through its containing domain.group.upgrade rather than carrying its own `realised-by` edge (like domain.value.kalide-owned-scaffold).
